messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC — i've been sketching an alternative to the current continuous-batcher that leans on 'cohort windows' instead of fixed microwindows. sounds similar to 'cohorts' we've mentioned but with a different enqueue contract.
ajay: curious, what's the main difference you want us to evaluate?
dana: +1, need to understand perf tradeoffs before we touch admission.
maria: the idea: each cohort is created lazily per tenant/shape and has an adaptive deadline computed from: recent latency percentiles + token budget. cohorts can merge if they overlap, and we allow soft preemption by credit.
chris: sounds like dynamic windows. how do you keep long-tail latency from spiking when cohorts merge?
maria: two levers: (1) cohort-level headroom tokens that reserve slots pre-merge, (2) an early-evict path for low-priority requests. evict path returns 429-ish fallback or routes to a cheaper model.
ajay: routing to cheaper model is nice but adds complexity. what's the expected overhead on the scheduler for tracking cohorts?
maria: moderately more metadata: cohort id, owner-lease timestamp, target-deadline, headroom-credit. we avoid global scans by storing cohorts in a sharded epoch map keyed by (tenant, size-shape).
leo: shard map sounds fine. how about KV cache interaction? cohort merging could invalidate warm-up assumptions.
dana: right — if cohorts merge we might lose prefix locality for the KV cache, causing model cold starts. any mitigation?
maria: plan: when merging, prefer merging cohorts with aligned KV prefixes. also introduce a 'warmup budget' token that forces a small early microbatch to populate KV without waiting for full cohort. basically pay a small throughput tax to keep cache hit-rate.
chris: can we simulate this quickly? a perf matrix showing cost vs tail-latency for different merge rates would help.
ajay: agree — we should also measure fairness (tenant starve risk) w/ headroom tokens. might need per-tenant cap on headroom.
leo: also watch memory pressure: cohort metadata + headroom tokens scales with number of cohorts. we can't let a noisy-tenant create millions. need eviction policies.
dana: eviction policy idea: LRU by last-activity with soft TTL, but protect requests currently in-flight.
maria: exactly. TTL + soft guard. also an emergency global cap that converts cohorts to lightweight placeholders (no headroom, no warmup).
chris: edge cases: what happens if a cohort's owner dies (OOM or node restart)?
maria: use lease heartbeats. if heartbeat fails > lease-grace, other shard picks up the cohort via 'steal' path and rehydrates minimal state from persistent cohort-index.
ajay: persistent index = small k-v store? that adds complexity but seems necessary for long-running cohorts. keep schema minimal.
dana: ok sounds workable. next steps: maria + ajay + leo to prototype a discrete-event sim that models: merge frequency, headroom sizes, KV hit-rate, memory overhead. chris will help define SLO knobs for tail latency.
maria: thanks — i'll post a short spec + sim plan later today. ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: please add feature-flag gating and metrics (cohort_count, merge_rate, headroom_allocated, evictions) before rollout. :gear:
leo: noted. i'll draft the metrics list.
maria: one more quick note — fallback policy should be orthogonal so we can A/B different cheap-models without scheduler change.
ajay: nice. that keeps surface area small.
chris: cool — meeting to review sim on Friday?
maria: yup, 10am PT. invite incoming. :calendar:
